name: Pop music
editorial_article: Pop music is a colossal and fluid genre of popular music that emerged in its distinct form during the mid-1950s within the United States and the United Kingdom. While the broader term "popular music" can encompass any music with mass appeal, the specific genre of "pop" has come to represent a highly curated, accessible, and often ephemeral musical style designed for broad consumption. Historically, pop and rock were once synonymous, but by the late 1960s, a divergence occurred: rock became increasingly associated with "album-oriented" artistic statements for adult audiences, while pop cemented itself as a singles-based format, often prioritizing immediate catchiness, slick production, and youth-oriented themes. \n\nThe sonic signature of pop is defined by its focus on accessibility and efficiency. Core structural elements typically include the standard verse-chorus arrangement, a relentless emphasis on hooks, and memorable melodies designed to stick in the listener's consciousness. Over the decades, pop has acted as a musical sponge, constantly absorbing and refining elements from disparate styles—ranging from rock, R&B, and hip-hop to electronic dance music and various regional folk traditions. This adaptability ensures that pop remains in a state of perpetual evolution, perpetually reflecting the contemporary zeitgeist of the urban middle class. In the 21st century, the definition of pop continues to stretch, embracing everything from bedroom-produced experiments to hyper-polished global stadium anthems, proving its status not just as a genre, but as the primary language of the modern music industry.

editorial_definition: Pop music is a commercial genre of popular music characterized by accessible song structures, strong hooks, and a focus on singles, designed for mass appeal across broad demographics.
